title: Evaluation of Cutaneous Sensory Function and Subcutaneous Tissue Changes Following Skin-Sparing Mastectomy: A Prospective, Controlled Clinical Study
summary:
What are we investigating?
In a skin-sparing mastectomy, diseased breast tissue is removed, but the outer skin of the breast is preserved to enable more attractive breast reconstruction later on. However, many patients report changes or reductions in sensation in the breast after the operation. We want to systematically investigate how skin sensation changes after this operation and whether it improves again over time.

How do we proceed?
We follow women who undergo skin-sparing mastectomy with immediate breast reconstruction for over a year. Before the operation and at several follow-up appointments, we perform painless tests:
Sensitivity tests: We check how well the skin senses touch, temperature, and light pressure.
Ultrasound examination: We measure the thickness of the subcutaneous fatty tissue.
Questionnaires: We ask patients to rate their own sensations and quality of life.

Why is this important?
The sense of touch in the breast is important for many women—not only for safety (e.g., feeling temperature), but also for well-being and satisfaction after surgery. So far, we still know too little about which surgical techniques better preserve sensation and how sensations develop over time.

What are the benefits of the study?
The results should help to improve surgical methods and better inform patients about the changes they can expect. Future patients could thus benefit from optimized treatment concepts that take into account both the cosmetic result and skin sensation.

Burden on participants:
The additional examinations are painless and take about 10-15 minutes per appointment. This does not change the medical treatment.

interventions.name:
Study arm: Prospective cohort study – patients after skin-sparing mastectomy
Description of intervention/exposure:
Patients undergoing skin-sparing mastectomy (SSM) with immediate breast reconstruction. Patients are treated according to their clinical indication and the surgical technique chosen b

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Women between the ages of 18 and 75
• Planned unilateral or bilateral SSM
• Planned immediate reconstruction
• No previous breast/thoracic wall surgery
• Capacity to give consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Pre-existing peripheral neuropathy/neurodegenerative diseases
• Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus/diabetic neuropathy
• Previous radiation therapy to the chest/thoracic wall
• Use of neurotoxic medications
